name: New Yorker Electronics
about:
New Yorker Electronics was established in 1948 in Northvale, New Jersey, initially serving the New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut area with a focus on capacitors. The company was incorporated in 1958 under the guidance of Abe Slivka and has remained family-owned since.

Today, New Yorker Electronics operates as an international distributor of electronic components, offering capacitors, resistors, semiconductors, connectors, filters, inductors, embedded solutions, power management products, and electromechanical devices. The company holds AS9120B and ISO 9001:2015 certifications and functions as a certified franchise distributor for nearly 100 manufacturers, including Vishay, Exxelia, and Cornell Dubilier Electronics. It operates in strict accordance with AS5553 and AS6496 standards to prevent counterfeit parts.

The company serves military, aerospace, and defense sectors, supplying the U.S. Department of Defense, Department of Justice, Navy, and major contractors such as Lockheed Martin, GE, Honeywell, General Dynamics, and BAE Systems. It is also a member of the Electronics Component Industry Association (ECIA) and the Electronic Resellers Association International (ERAI).

New Yorker Electronics differentiates itself by maintaining heightened military and aerospace performance levels across its operations and by implementing rigorous anti-counterfeit standards (AS5553 and AS6496) into everyday practices.
